cards.text: Zechariah is a prophet to God's people, and they're rebuilding the house of God in Jerusalem (Zechariah 1:1; Ezra 5:1-2). He's just seen four chariots ride out in a vision (Zechariah 6:1-8), and now the word of the LORD comes to him again. No horses this time, friend, just a TO-DO LIST.

Step one: take an offering from three exiles who have arrived from Babylon: Heldai, Tobijah and Jedaiah. Babylon to Jerusalem is a LONG road, friend, and these three still come with something to give.

cards.question: Zechariah's next stop is the house of Josiah son of Zephaniah. True or false: God tells him to go there that same day.

cards.text: Next, God tells Zechariah to take silver and gold and make something ornate. Me? I spent YEARS under takeout menus in a junk drawer, and NOBODY ever called me ornate.

cards.question: God's plan for that silver and gold: make an ornate ___.
The ornate silver and gold crown is ready. Whose head does Zechariah set it on?

cards.text: So the crown goes on Joshua son of Jehozadak, the high priest. Then Zechariah is to tell him what the LORD of Hosts says: 'Here is a man whose name is the Branch, and He will branch out from His place…'

cards.question: God's people are rebuilding right now. So what will the man called the Branch do? He will build the ___ of the LORD.

cards.text: Then it comes AGAIN: 'Yes, He will build the temple of the LORD; He will be clothed in splendor and will sit on His throne and rule.' When I repeat myself it's because I forgot, but when God repeats Himself, friend, you LEAN IN.

cards.question: The Branch will sit on His throne and rule. What else will He be, right there on that throne?
Right after the priest on the throne comes one more line. Fill it in: there will be ___ counsel between the two.

cards.text: The crown becomes a memorial to Helem, Tobijah, Jedaiah and the gracious son of Zephaniah. The Millers carved MY name into my handle, but these folks get remembered with a CROWN, so same idea, WAY shinier.

cards.question: That memorial crown has to live somewhere. Where does it stay?

answers.text: In the temple of the LORD

cards.text: Then the message turns to the crew who will build the temple of the LORD. My whole bakery runs on invitations, friend, so I am VERY interested in who's on this crew.

cards.question: True or false: people from far away will come and build the temple of the LORD.

cards.text: And when it happens, here's the line: 'you will know that the LORD of Hosts has sent Me to you.' But hold up, friend, because there's an IF.

cards.question: All this about the temple and those far away comes with a condition. What is it?

answers.text: If they diligently obey the LORD's voice
If they faithfully keep the Sabbath day
If they gladly give their silver and gold

findings.problem: "These three still come with something to give" goes beyond the text. Zechariah 6:10 has God telling Zechariah to take an offering from the exiles. It never says Heldai, Tobijah and Jedaiah came to give it. The line is also a pleasant observation more than a real laugh.

rule.text: Don't stretch the text. Exaggerate only in his own jokes.

findings.problem: Joshua is never mentioned before this card, so the baker can't reason out whose head gets the crown. The only name they've seen is Josiah, which is a wrong answer, and Zerubbabel looks like the natural guess for a crown. Cards 3 and 5 are already discovery questions, and this makes three in a row near the start of the stop.

rule.text: Before each choice card, Papa Dorin's story card gives enough context that the baker can reason their way to the answer.

findings.problem: The question asks the baker to supply the next words of a line: "Right after the priest on the throne comes one more line. Fill it in: there will be ___ counsel between the two." That tests wording they haven't seen, not the meaning of the passage.

rule.text: Never ask the baker to guess the next words of a line.

findings.problem: "And when it happens" turns the knowing into something that follows the building. Zechariah 6:15 only joins the two with "and."

rule.text: Leave open what the text leaves open: who is being spoken to, why, or how two things connect.

findings.problem: The card quotes 'you will know that the LORD of Hosts has sent Me to you' without saying who "Me" is. papa-dorin.md says to name a speaker who says "I" before quoting him. The text doesn't make clear who "Me" is: it could be Zechariah, or it could be a divine speaker, given the BSB's capital M. The rule to leave open what the text leaves open points the other way.
findings.question: When a quoted "I" or "Me" is unclear in the text, should Papa Dorin name a speaker, leave the speaker open, or avoid quoting the line?

findings.problem: The right answer says "If they diligently obey," and the question attaches the condition to "the temple and those far away." Together they suggest that those far away are the ones who must obey. Zechariah 6:15 says "if you diligently obey," and "This will happen" doesn't say exactly what it covers. The card changes who is being spoken to.

rule.text: Call things what the text calls them.
